A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPS/SCF calibration study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original calibration and error-detection experiments on SPIDER and BIRD, including benchmark results, sampling ablations, difficulty analyses, and examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds calibration-data and sampling sensitivity experiments, coefficient analyses, and feature-removal ablations.

M1.justification: The MPS mapping, SCF extraction and matching, aggregate product feature, and nucleus/beam sampling procedure are retained. Appendix B's Algorithms 1–3 are substantively unchanged; the new feature-removal experiments evaluate components rather than revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate English text-to-SQL calibration and error detection on SPIDER and BIRD. The added experiments vary calibration-data quantities, sampling counts, and features within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The uncalibrated-probability and Platt-scaling comparators remain unchanged. The comparison using model probabilities, perplexity, P(True), and verbalized confidence is retained from v1 Table 2 as v2 Table 4, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: New supplemental protocols vary calibration-set fractions down to 1/64, output counts across k = 1, 3, 5, and 10, and individual feature removals. Primary splits, models, and metrics remain unchanged. Section 7.4's statement that the experiments use k = 5 conflicts with the retained k = 10 in Section 5.3 and Appendix C.2, so an actual primary-setting change is not established.

E4.justification: Section 7.4 adds sensitivity tests addressing calibration-data requirements and sampling budgets. Appendix A adds standardized coefficient analyses and systematic removal of individual sub-clause feature groups, including AGG, on both datasets with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. These substantially extend the earlier sampling-method, difficulty, and probability-shift analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2 explicitly averages the calibration-size experiment over ten random runs, whereas v1 reports single-run evaluation. This does not establish additional runs for retained results. No variability estimates or inferential significance tests are added; Tables 12–13 highlight effect magnitudes using a stated 0.005 threshold.

E6.justification: The main benchmark table and matched earlier appendix results are unchanged, but Tables 2–3 and 10–13 add substantial sensitivity, coefficient, and feature-ablation findings. For example, the new BIRD calibration-size study reports AUC declining from 0.737 to 0.627 at 1/64 of the calibration data, while Table 13 reports a −0.017 AUC change when SELECT features are removed. These are new experimental findings, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the suggested calibration-sample requirement of Ω(m²) with approximately 10m, citing Hsu and Mazumdar (2024). This changes the quantitative sample-complexity rationale for avoiding overfitting. The calibration definitions and method equations remain unchanged, and no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: benchmarking post-hoc text-to-SQL calibration, proposing MPS with SCF signals, and improving calibration and error detection. The added analyses support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning calibration-data scarcity, sampling-budget tradeoffs, and the roles of individual features. Appendix A attributes AGG's importance to combining information across sub-clauses and discusses dataset-dependent SELECT and WHERE effects. The existing language, inference-cost, and zero-shot limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The added analyses document their sampling grids and aggregation of standardized coefficients into signed and absolute weight sums. Appendix B also corrects ORDERED BY to ORDER BY, consistent with the existing pseudocode. Prompts, software settings, hardware, runtimes, and resource links otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hsu and Mazumdar (2024) for logistic-regression sample complexity, Naeini et al. (2015) for ECE, and Nixon et al. (2019) for ACE. The substantive positioning relative to earlier calibration and semantic-parsing work is retained.

P1.justification: The narrative receives localized editing and restructuring: the former appendix base-score discussion becomes Section 7.5, Section 7.4 is added, some appendix subheadings are simplified, and wording, author spelling, and acknowledgements are corrected. Most existing prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The presentation substantially expands with dedicated calibration-size and sampling-count tables, coefficient-ranking tables, and feature-removal delta tables. The former appendix base-score table moves into the main text in a narrower format, and surrounding tables reflow. All five existing figure graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new sensitivity and feature-removal analyses provide useful evidence about data requirements, sampling budgets, and which SCF components matter. These strengthen understanding of the retained method without changing its headline results. The benefit is limited by missing variability estimates and the new k = 5 statement conflicting with the retained k = 10 setup, leaving some practical guidance ambiguous.
